newsitem.title: UK: LME copper moves up, nudges $2,250 in late London.
newsitem.headline: LME copper moves up, nudges $2,250 in late London.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three months copper advanced in a flurry of late inter-office activity to nudge next resistance now seen at $2,250 per tonne. Copper was bid at $2,245 when Comex closed at 1900 GMT, sharply up even from the firmer kerb close of $2,221 which was stronger by $26 from Monday.
Brokers said copper had continued to attract interest in late London business after rallying during the day once it had shrugged off a build in LME warehouse stocks.

Nearby tightness in the West overshadowed news of a build of almost 11,500 tonnes. Most of that went to Singapore. Resistance for copper is now pegged at $2,250 and then the November 28 high of $2,313. Aluminium finished the kerb $8.50 firmer at $1,560.50 and by 1900 GMT, helped up by copper, was confronting important resistance which brokers said was at $1,570.
